title: FamilyMart Introduces New Dress Code for Workers
paragraphs: FamilyMart, one of Japan's biggest convenience store chains, has introduced new rules about how its workers can look. Under the new rules, staff can now choose their own hair color, and Muslim women are allowed to wear hijabs.

The company announced the changes on August 26, 2026, and they started on September 1. The new rules are called "FamilyMart Coordinate." As well as removing rules about hair color, they give staff more freedom in how they wear their uniform. For example, workers can wear other clothes in layers with it. Staff can also use a working name, written in Japanese hiragana or katakana, on their name badge.

At the same time, FamilyMart introduced new uniforms. It is the first time in 10 years that the company has fully changed its uniform. The old jacket-style uniform has been replaced by a T-shirt. According to FamilyMart, this is a first for the convenience store industry in Japan. There is also a long-sleeved version. The T-shirts are made of thick cotton and come in sizes from XS to 11L. The design is based on a T-shirt from FamilyMart's own clothing brand, Convenience Wear. The new uniforms will be worn at about 16,500 stores across Japan.

FamilyMart says that staff asked for clothes that are easier to move in and more casual. The company also wants to have a more diverse group of workers and wants to become the most attractive convenience store to work for. To help hire more people, it will also start using recorded and online job interviews.

Not everyone online liked the changes. Some people said that the new style was a bit too casual. Others said that hair color was not important, and that they cared more about how workers treat customers.
